description:
FILED s470bk (Opus, 2026-09-05) with the discriminating measurement already
taken, while shipping #1001 half (a).

THE MEASUREMENT.  `for my $i (1 .. 4000000) { $n *= 3; $n %= 1000003 }`,
emitted as `(p-foreach-range-raw ($i 1 4000000) (p-*=-raw $n 3)
(p-%=-raw $n 1000003))`, best-of-5 interleaved against a `92a568e` worktree,
PCL startup measured separately at 0.157 s:

  whole process   before 0.172 s   after 0.188 s   (+9.4 %)
  the LOOP alone  before 0.015 s   after 0.031 s   (roughly DOUBLED)
  perl 5.40.3     0.111 s total, 0.106 s of loop

So PCL still beats perl on this loop by 3.4x where it beat it by 7x.  The
cost is 8 million guard evaluations (two compound ops x 4 M iterations) for
16 ms = ~2 ns each, and it is the price of `$obj *= 3` reaching its `*`
handler at all (#1001(a): four compound ops had NO overload dispatch).

WHAT THE GUARD IS.  `%compound-arith-form` emits
`(if (and *p-any-overload-registered* (and (p-box-p CUR) (p-box-class CUR)))
     (slow CUR DELTA) (INLINE-ARITHMETIC))`
and the RAW twin (`p-*=-raw`, `p-%=-raw`, `p-incf-raw`, ...) carries it too.

THE QUESTION: can the RAW twin's guard be retired when the DELTA is a
compile-time number?  The raw twin is emitted only where the compiler gave
the slot a raw-numeric VERDICT (docs/raw-numeric-verdict.md), and the checked
coercion DECLINES the freeze rather than storing a box â so a raw-verdict
slot may be provably never a p-box, which would make `(p-box-p CUR)` dead
code and the guard removable for a literal delta.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE HERE.  Two reasons, both worth writing down:
  1. The claim is a COMPILER guarantee and this was a `cl/`-only commit â the
     runtime cannot see the verdict, and getting it wrong is a SILENT WRONG of
     exactly the archetype kind (`$obj *= 3` numifying again).
  2. `p-incf-raw` / `p-decf-raw` have carried the same guard since #972 for
     the same reason, and #1001's task text records the measurement that put
     it there: `my $s = 0; $s += $obj` emits `(p-incf-raw $s $o)` with an
     OVERLOADED DELTA and the slot then HOLDS the object.  That measurement is
     about the DELTA, not the slot, which is why a LITERAL delta is the
     interesting case and the two must be separated before anything changes.

THE ORDER QUESTION IS ALREADY ANSWERED, do not re-try it: putting the
`(p-box-p â¦)` test BEFORE `*p-any-overload-registered*` (the order
`%p-no-overload-possible-p`'s comment argues for) was measured on the same
loop at 0.1859 s against 0.1893 s flag-first â inside both spreads, so it
does not distinguish them, and #972's five-candidate table stands.  The
attempt and its numbers are in `%compound-arith-form`'s own comment.

BAR when taken: whether the raw-numeric verdict PROVES the slot is never a
p-box (read `%pcl-to-number-raw`'s decline path and Pl/VarAnnotator's write
family), a probe that puts an overloaded object into a raw-verdict slot by
every route the corpus contains, the bench above, the gate, and the full
sweep.  A guard removed on a wrong premise is not visible in any of the
runners â it is a wrong VALUE.

=== RULED s470 (Fable): emitter-side, perf agent round 27, L4 ===
The correctness fix STAYS; the guard-free path is a PERF lever, not a revert.
For a RAW twin whose DELTA is a compile-time literal number (`$n *= 3`,
`$n %= 1000003`, `$s += 1`) the only question left is whether CUR is a blessed
box, and a raw-numeric-verdict slot cannot hold one â the checked coercion
DECLINES the freeze rather than storing a box.  The EMITTER knows both facts,
so it emits a guard-free variant (`:delta-literal t`, or a `-raw-lit` twin);
that makes it an EMISSION change, which is why it was out of scope for the
`cl/`-only commit that filed this.
ACCEPTANCE = the measurement above: the 4e6 `*=`/`%=` loop back to ~0.015 s of
loop time (0.172 s of process), with `.=` and the BOXED `+=` shape unmoved.

=== DONE (s470bn, 2026-09-05) ===
SHIPPED as task #1183, commit `3f24edc` (Kind-A `numeric-slot`).
ACCEPTANCE MET: the 4e6 `*=`/`%=` loop 0.0331 s -> 0.0135 s (-59.2 %, ceiling
-62.5 %, control pair +0.2 %); `.=`, the boxed `+=` and `intloop+=` are
EMISSION-IDENTICAL under the switch, which is the "unmoved" half.

AND THE RULED PREMISE WAS FALSE, which is the finding.  A raw slot CAN hold a
blessed box, by TWO routes, both probed:
  * a raw compound write with a NON-literal delta â `my $s = 0; $s += $obj`
    leaves the OBJECT in the slot, so a later `$s *= 3` has a literal delta and
    a BLESSED current value.  Licensing on the delta alone numifies it.
  * a B-regime write â %pcl-to-number-strict DECLINES the freeze and stores
    `(p-box-init V)`, i.e. a box, exactly when the value is overload-capable.
So the licence had to be about the SLOT, not the site: VarAnnotator's `numonly`
(every write stores a compile-time NUMBER; NOT "num-FAMILY", since `$x = $a +
$obj` is num-family and yields an object).  Both routes are runtime rows in
Pl/t/perf-levers-01.t.

WHAT THE GUARD COSTS IS THE BRANCH, NOT ITS TESTS â measured, and it is why the
shape was obvious once seen: each HALF of the guard alone cost as much as the
whole (box-test-only 0.028 s, flag-read-only 0.030 s, guard 0.029 s on the same
loop).  With the branch gone SBCL compiles the body as straight-line arithmetic.
subject: MEASURED +9.4% (loop-only ~2x) on a raw `*=`/`%=` loop from #1001(a)\x27s overload guard - can the RAW twin retire it when the delta is a literal number and the slot carries a raw-numeric verdict?
